name: NASA DONKI
gives: Real solar flares, space-ray storms and magnetic storms. Storm cards and Today’s Sun.
note: Archive pulled 12 Nov 2026. One radiation-storm record exists per detector, so we count storms, not records.

name: NOAA SWPC + GOES
gives: How strong each storm’s space rays were (S1 to S5) and the shape of the storm.
note: Measured at Earth’s distance from the Sun. The Moon is at about the same distance, so we use it as a stand-in for a Moon base.

name: NASA BVAD (2022)
gives: How much air, water and food one astronaut uses each day.
note: We turn kilograms into bars a child can read.

name: NASA’s 9 candidate landing regions
gives: The 9 places you can choose near the Moon’s South Pole.
note: These are candidate regions, not a landing plan. Centres are read off NASA’s map, so they are approximate.

name: LRO LOLA maps
gives: How sunny each region is, and how often Earth is in view.
note: These are long-term averages, not a calendar. The game spreads sunny days and Earth-view days evenly to match each region’s share.

name: NASA OSDR
gives: Real lab findings about what space rays do to living things.
licence: NASA open data; cite each paper
note: Yeast and mice in a lab. Not results for people.
